overview: This file documents the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers’ regulation and expansion of occupied Japan’s international telecommunications between November 1947 and March 1948. Its despatches, SCAP directives, explanatory memorandum, and detailed rate enclosure address payment rules for radiotelegraph traffic with Europe, monthly accounting for American carriers, the extension of overseas radiotelephone service through the United States, divisions of revenue among carriers, and the technical authorization of a Japanese radiotelegraph newscast service. Together they show how telecommunications policy was being used both to reintegrate Japan into international communications and to protect its scarce foreign-exchange position.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1420 on payment for messages over European circuits
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards SCAPIN 1823 establishing prepaid and collect-payment rules for press and governmental messages between Japan and Sweden, Switzerland, and Russia.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1420: incoming European press/government messages must be prepaid, outgoing ones sent collect, building foreign-exchange credit for Japan rather than yen payments; Soviet Council member and diplomatic missions were asked to inform their governments.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1823 on payment for Japan–Europe messages
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Japanese Government, through the Central Liaison Office, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The directive orders the Japanese Ministry of Communications to apply new payment rules to press and government traffic on direct circuits with Sweden, Switzerland, and Russia.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1823 (Dec. 1947): Japan-to-Europe messages go collect, incoming prepaid; Communications Ministry barred from nonconforming traffic, with direct SCAP-ministry technical contact authorized.

subfiles.title: Explanatory memorandum on SCAPIN 1823
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Recipients of SCAPIN 1823 other than the Japanese Government
subfiles.about: The memorandum explains the history and foreign-exchange rationale behind the new payment arrangements for three European radiotelegraph circuits.
subfiles.summary: Memo explains Japan's Sweden/Switzerland circuits ran through the war; reversing payment direction lets Japan earn foreign-currency credits instead of paying yen, improving its exchange position.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 94 on monthly accounting for American carriers
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards SCAPIN 1228/7 revising the accounting and deposit schedule for telecommunications involving American carriers.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 94: directive requires monthly (not semimonthly) Communications Ministry accounting for U.S.-Japan and Manila-Japan telecommunications, forwarded to State in five copies.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1228/7 revising telecommunications accounting
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Japanese Government, through the Central Liaison Office, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The directive changes telecommunications statements and deposits for traffic with the United States and Manila from semimonthly to monthly submission.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1228/7 (Feb. 1948): Ministry of Communications must submit monthly preliminary statements, deposits, and final accounts for U.S. and Manila telecommunications within 30 days, reporting certificate collections within five days.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 163 on overseas radiotelephone service
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards SCAPIN 1830/2 authorizing additional radiotelephone calls between Japan and foreign countries through the United States.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 163 reports a new directive authorizing expanded Japan overseas radiotelephone service via the U.S. from March 1948, under specified conditions.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1830/2 authorizing expanded radiotelephone service
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The directive authorizes radiotelephone service between Japan and listed foreign points via the United States and establishes operational and accounting conditions.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1830/2 extends radiotelephone rules to added destinations and authorizes Japan-Hawaii collect calls from March 15, 1948, with Eighth Army and SCAP overseeing operations and accounting.

subfiles.title: Rates and division of revenue for radiotelephone service
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Japanese Government, as an enclosure to SCAPIN 1830/2
subfiles.about: The enclosure supplies weekday and Sunday telephone rates and divides revenue among Japan, AT&T, and other carriers for service routed through the United States.
subfiles.summary: Rate schedule sets Japan Zone A/B radiotelephone rates ($15 weekday, $12 Sunday) to Alaska, Caribbean, Europe, Ecuador, and Panama, dividing revenue among Japan, AT&T, and foreign carriers, with Alaska rate zones and overtime/report charges detailed.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 200 on radiotelegraph newscasts
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards SCAPIN 1215/1 revising the technical authorization for radiotelegraph newscasts from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 200 forwards a March directive amending 1946 newscast rules, proposing self-explanatory directives be sent without covering despatches going forward.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1215/1 authorizing radiotelegraph newscast frequencies
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The directive replaces an earlier technical provision with new frequencies, power limits, emission type, and coverage areas for Japanese radiotelegraph newscasts.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1215/1 authorizes Japanese radiotelegraph newscasts on three frequencies at up to 10 kilowatts, beamed toward East Asia and the South China Sea.

interest: Shows postwar rebuilding of Japan's international communications, with detailed telephone-revenue sharing and foreign-exchange payment rules.
